summary: Powell County, MT L-4 cab on Arrastra Mountain, built 1930 and abandoned by 1956; removal date unknown and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Abandoned by 1956; the association says it is unclear when the cab was removed

events.note: L-4 cab built in 1930 per FFLA; Missoula newspaper reported the new station on July 22, 1930
Independent Record: a plane contracted that year would replace the lookout (a plan, not a confirmed end of staffing)
FFLA: abandoned by 1956; removal date unknown

evidence.supports: elevation 7,976 ft; about 10 miles northwest of Lincoln, Powell County
L-4 cab built 1930; abandoned by 1956; removal date unclear
evidence.quote: This L-4 cab, built in 1930, was abandoned by 1956. It's unclear when it was removed.

evidence.supports: association lists the site under Lolo/Helena National Forests
another listing places the site in Powell County, Helena National Forest
site listed as a ground-type record, gone
1930 newspaper: new lookout station located near the source of Arrastra Creek, about 8,000 feet
evidence.quote: Perched 8,000 feet above sea level near the source of Arrastra creek, in the upper Blackfoot valley, a new lookout station has been located for added fire protection

evidence.supports: station to serve land added to the Missoula forest two years earlier
evidence.quote: will serve the large acreage added to the Missoula forest two years ago.

evidence.supports: station would let the observer watch three drainages
evidence.quote: permitting the observer to watch the Arrastra, Dry and Meadow creek drainages

evidence.supports: nine miles of telephone line to be built; lookout to take station after the line is finished
evidence.quote: Nine miles of telephone line will be built to the new lookout and as soon as it is completed, the lookout will take his station on top of the hill.

evidence.supports: 1948 report: plane contracted to replace the lookout
evidence.quote: The plane contracted this year will replace the lookout formerly on Arrastra peak.

evidence.supports: 1948 supervisor's reason: packing supplies hard; aerial detection sometimes cheaper than lookout towers
evidence.quote: Because of difficulty in packing supplies to back-country lookouts, aerial detection of forest fires in some cases has proven more economical than keeping men in lookout towers

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1930 newspaper calls the land part of the Missoula forest. The association lists Lolo/Helena National Forests and another listing says Helena National Forest. The record keeps Helena National Forest, the agency on the current listing.

A 1948 newspaper reports a plane would replace the lookout; the association gives abandonment by 1956 and no removal date. The 1948 item describes a plan, so it is recorded as an 'other' event and not as the end of staffing.

sources.title: Arrastra Mountain - Forest Lookouts (quoting The Daily Missoulian, 1930, and Independent Record, 1948)

notes_for_editor: Few sources. The FFLA page credits a 'Fire Lookout Museum' photo with no image URL in the cache, so no photo was added. No source describes the site today; the brief's status 'gone' is supported. The 1930 newspaper says the lookout would take his station after the telephone line was built; no staffing names were found, so no staffed events are recorded. Two web searches were used.
